test.name: Single record already in hand should route to extraction, not start a search
test.description: The user has already captured an individual record page and wants its contents extracted into the research files. That is extraction's job — search-external-sites' capture-analysis step is the triage of a results LIST, and even that hands selected records to extraction. The skill's description carves this out ('Do NOT use when the user wants to analyze a single record already in context').

input.user_message: I've saved the individual record page for Patrick Flynn from the Ancestry search as a PDF — extract the names, dates, and places from it into the research files.

negative.explanation: A single captured record page going into the research files is extraction (`extraction_append` for a FamilySearch record, the record-structurer agent for any other source). search-external-sites generates search URLs and triages results lists; its own workflow passes selected records to the record-structurer agent. Re-firing search-external-sites here would either re-search (wrong) or duplicate extraction (also wrong). Since extraction became a tool call and an agent rather than a skill, no skill is the correct route, so this is an out-of-scope negative (`correct_skill: []`): the skill under test must stay out of extraction, and any correct extraction path passes (genealogist ruling 2026-09-30, option B).

judge_context: This is a grade_on_invariant negative test: PASS/FAIL is decided solely by the deterministic no-search-no-write validator (no external_links_search call, no new external_site log entry). Routing and activation are NOT gated. The judge runs base-only and diagnostically here — its scores do not decide the outcome.

Ideal behavior is to hand the already-captured single record to extraction (an `extraction_append` or `@plugin:record-structurer` call, or a one-line hand-off) rather than generating a new search URL or re-triaging the record itself. Note in your rationale whether the skill routed cleanly.

Known model prior (why this was previously flaky, issue #1519): the model's decline is correct nearly every run, but its phrasing varies — a decline that engages with the request ("upload the PDF and I'll hand it to extraction") was read by the activation heuristic as substantive output and failed the test, while a terser hand-off passed. Every deterministic input was identical across the passing and failing runs. Under grade_on_invariant the decline phrasing no longer decides the outcome; only executing or logging an external-site search does.

Extraction writes its own non-external_site log entry for the record it was handed. That is extraction doing its own job, not harm, and the validator is scoped to external_site entries for exactly that reason.
